Theme

Money, work & business · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

due adjective

owed; payable on a set day

also owed, owing, payable, owe, due date, fall due

classical

Cic. Att. 14.18.1: Kal. Jān. dēbuit, adhūc nōn solvit
Cic. Fam. 3.5.4: pecūnia … quae mihi ex pūblicā permūtātiōne dēbētur

1With an infinitive, dēbeō speaks of a duty, never of what is merely expected to happen: Lewis & Short, in classical prose always of moral necessity. Ruling: dēbeō is for duty.

dēbeō1, dēbēre, dēbuī, dēbitum

verb, second conjugation

owe; in the passive, be owed, be due

“It is due” is the passive, dēbētur; what is due, dēbitum.

Other words

  • diēs, diēī f. — the due date, the day set

    noun, fifth declension; feminine in this sense · also used · classical · Caes. BG 6.33.4: quam ad diem eī legiōnī … dēbērī frūmentum sciēbat; Caes. BG 1.8.3: ubi ea diēs quam cōnstituerat cum lēgātīs vēnit

    A day fixed in advance, for a payment, a meeting or a hearing, is feminine (Lewis & Short; see day).

Examples

  • Kal. Jān. dēbuit, adhūc nōn solvit

    the money was due on the first of January, and he still hasn’t paidCic. Att. 14.18.1

  • quam ad diem eī legiōnī quae in praesidiō relinquēbātur dēbērī frūmentum sciēbat

    the day on which, as he knew, corn was due to the legion left on guardCaes. BG 6.33.4

See also debt, pay, bill, day.
